item.title: Steelers’ Latest Trade Buzz Would Add Another Weapon for Aaron Rodgers
item.description: The Pittsburgh Steelers and quarterback Aaron Rodgers have looked the part of a potential contender in the AFC so far this season. Through the first six weeks of the year, the team holds a 4-2 record. Rodgers has played well in what he has said will be his final NFL season. He has completed 61.4 percent of his pass attempts for 1,487 yards, 12 touchdowns, and five interceptions. While the team has played decent football this season, the Steelers could still use more help. One area of need comes at wide receiver, where the team has performed under expectations. All of that being said, Pittsburgh has been connected to a potential trade that would add another weapon for Rodgers. Sep 27, 2026; Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, USA; Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers (8) throws the ball against the Cincinnati Bengals during the second half at Acrisure Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Barry Reeger-Imagn Images Pittsburgh Steelers Linked to Intriguing Trade for New Wide Receiver The Athletic has named the Steelers as a potential trade destination for Tennessee Titans wideout Calvin Ridley. In addition to Pittsburgh, they listed the Las Vegas Raiders and Seattle Seahawks as potential trade suitors for Ridley as well. “Ridley took a pay cut this offseason to remain with the Titans. The Tennessee offense has been dysfunctional under coordinator Brian Daboll. Ridley had only five catches on 10 targets through the first six weeks of the season. He has been out-snapped by rookie Carnell Tate, free-agent addition Wan’Dale Robinson and second-year receiver Elic Ayomanor. Ridley does not have any guaranteed money on his deal after this year,” they wrote . “There is some meat on the bone with Ridley. The route running and releases are still NFL quality. He was wide open for a touchdown in Week 6 against the Colts, and quarterback Cam Ward missed him. Ridley could still make an impact with better quarterback play and overall offensive infrastructure.” So far this season, Ridley has barely had a role within the Titans’ offense. He has caught five passes for 81 yards. Last season, he racked up 303 receiving yards and no scores on 17 receptions. Back in the 2024 campaign, the 31-year-old wideout showed off what he’s capable of producing. He caught 64 passes for 1,017 yards and four touchdowns. Expect to continue hearing rumors about the Steelers as the November 10 trade deadline draws closer. Ridley is a name worth monitoring as a potential trade candidate, although no concrete reporting has connected Pittsburgh to him. item.title: Leclerc sets Austin practice pace from Verstappen
item.description: Charles Leclerc won the US Grand Prix in Austin two years ago [Getty Images] Ferrari's Charles Leclerc set the pace from Red Bull's Max Verstappen in first practice at the United States Grand Prix. Leclerc was 0.084 seconds quicker than Verstappen at the start of the first weekend on which Mercedes driver Kimi Antonelli can clinch his first world title. The Italian was fifth fastest, 0.481secs off the pace, behind McLaren's Lando Norris and Mercedes' George Russell. Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton was sixth ahead of McLaren's Oscar Piastri. Antonelli will win the championship in Austin only if he wins the race and Russell finishes below eighth and Hamilton below fourth. Mercedes have reverted both their cars to the upgraded specification that was introduced in Malaysia two races ago but about which there remain questions over its relative performance. The team believe that the upgrade has more performance within it, but that they have not yet found the appropriate set-up to maximise it. They hope a full, 'normal' weekend with three practice sessions will enable them to hone it. Ferrari have an upgrade here which is fundamentally a new floor. Both Leclerc and Hamilton played down its potential impact. Hamilton said: "We have a very, very small upgrade this weekend. It's less than a tenth. It's like half a tenth. "So, I don't think that propels us forward enough to necessarily challenge that deficit. But maybe the track suits our car, and maybe they'll have a one-off weekend. Maybe Mercedes will have an off weekend again, and we'll be right there to take it." item.title: MotoGP Academy Puts a Badge on Racing Schools Worldwide. The Fine Print Is Where It Gets Interesting
item.description: MotoGP Sepang 2024 03. Image credit: Renek78/Wikimedia Commons (CC0) MotoGP has found a cheap way to scout riders in places where it has no pipeline: put its name on other people’s racing schools. The MotoGP Academy, announced on motogp.com on 21 October under the Road to MotoGP banner, is a seal of approval for racing schools and institutions that meet the championship’s standards on and off the track. How the scheme works Each Academy is named after its nation, region or continent, following the naming model of the FIM MotoMini World Series. Larger countries can have several, while smaller ones may have a single national hub. The stated focus is key markets and places with strong growth potential, and the stated aim is a global network of elite schools, especially where the sport is underserved. To qualify, a school must meet requirements in four areas: infrastructure, training methodology, technical execution and brand visibility. In return MotoGP says it will invest directly in each academy’s success, with toolkits, activation support, branding and discounts on MotoGP products. Interested schools start by emailing info@motogpacademy.com. Read the criteria, not the headline Three of those four boxes are about whether a school is any good. The fourth is about how well it advertises MotoGP. That is not a criticism, because a promoter that wants a presence in a new market has to get its name in front of local families somehow, and a badge on an existing school is far cheaper than building one. It does mean the scheme is best read as a licensing and marketing programme with a coaching standard attached, not as MotoGP running its own schools. Racing at Phillip Island, which MotoGP leaves for Adelaide after this weekend. File image. Photo: Ken So / Unsplash. What the announcement leaves open The announcement does not set out rider age limits, fees or application deadlines, and it does not name a first batch of academies or markets. Those details decide whether the badge means something. A parent comparing two schools will want to know what the standard actually tests and who checks it, and a school will want to know what the support costs. Why the timing makes sense MotoGP is spending a lot of effort on geography. Malaysia has been confirmed on the calendar from 2027 to 2031, and the championship leaves Phillip Island after this weekend for a new era in Adelaide. Sepang, the Malaysian venue, has a long history we looked at earlier today . Local riders help sell a race to local fans and sponsors, and an existing school is the quickest place to find one. With the 2027 grid already full , any rider this scheme produces is years from the grid, so treat it as a long-term bet rather than a quick fix. What to watch Watch for the first named academies and the markets they sit in, and whether MotoGP publishes the standards schools will be measured against. Until then, this is a promising badge with the hard questions left for later. Lead image: Image credit:

item.title: Barcelona star reveals why he is getting ‘tired’ of Real Madrid ahead of El Clásico
item.description: Barcelona star reveals why he is getting ‘tired’ of Real Madrid ahead of El Clásico Barcelona star Fermín López has this week opened up on his frustration with those in a position of power at arch rivals Real Madrid. This of course comes as Spanish football’s two biggest clubs prepare to lock horns for the latest occasion this coming weekend. Barcelona are primed to welcome Real Madrid to the Spotify Camp Nou on Sunday evening, for the season’s first edition of El Clásico. Heading into the fixture, much of the discourse has centered on the ongoing ‘Negreira Case’, a long-standing point of contention between the respective boards at Real and Barca. The former recently breathed fresh life into the investigation into the Blaugrana’s long-term payments to ex-La Liga referee chief José María Enríquez Negreira, upon sending a massive document featuring files, figures and more to UEFA. Barcelona, all the while, maintain their innocence, adamant that they have done no wrong, culminating in mounting tension between the clubs ahead of Sunday’s clash on the pitch. Speaking in an exchange with the media on Friday, the aforementioned Fermín López therefore made use of the opportunity to reveal his disappointment with the behaviour of Florentino Pérez and co. During an interview with Teledeporte of TVE, midfielder Fermín admitted: “Real Madrid’s constant references to the Negreira case are getting a bit tiring because we’re showing our quality on the pitch. It’s unfair to engage in this kind of rhetoric when things are going well for us. If they keep pushing this narrative, it’s because it suits them, but we don’t get involved in it.” Conor Laird – GSFN

item.title: Why Rays' key to World Series victory might revolve around Jacob Misiorowski
item.description: Why Rays' key to World Series victory might revolve around Jacob Misiorowski originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Tampa Bay Rays are facing the Milwaukee Brewers in the 2026 MLB World Series, and after the Brewers swept the reining champions in four games in the NLCS, the Brewers are favorites in this matchup. They also have home-field advantage, which makes the Rays' task a lot harder. But there's certainly a path for the Rays to win it all. But how can they actually win the World Series? ESPN's Alden Gonzalez highlighted how the Brewers have a vulnerable starting rotation, led by Jacob Misiorowski, and that if the Rays can chase him out of the game early, the Rays could be set up for a lot of success in the World Series. Rays can beat Brewers by getting after Jacob Misiorowski "To beat the Brewers, you have to take advantage of their starting rotation," Gonzalez writes. "It begins with running up the pitch counts of their two front-line starters, Jacob Misiorowski and Logan Henderson." If the Rays are able to make the Brewers' top-two starting pitchers throw a lot of pitches early in games, making it so they don't last long in their respective starts, they can have a real chance of winning it all. It might seem like a simple thing to chase a pitcher early, but considering the Brewers' top-heavy bullpen, getting to the middle of the bullpen might prove to be a key to this series. Besides, in Games 3 and 4, Milwaukee will be relying on more of their bullpen, with starters Dustin May, Shane Drohan, and Robert Gasser set to be involved. If the Rays can force the Brewers to the bullpen early in Games 1 and 2, they could set themselves up nicely for the rest of the series. MORE : Dodgers facing tricky question over Shohei Ohtani's future as a two-way player As Gonzalez put it, "scoring early will be a must for the Rays." They can win the World Series even if they struggle against Misiorowski and Henderson, but if they have success against them, their odds of winning the series will increase significantly. The snowball effect of chasing Misiorowski and/or Henderson from a game early would be huge. Taxing the Brewers' bullpen is the key to the Rays' success, and to do so, they're going to have to get after Misiorowski. Games 1 and 2 might be a telling outcome for how the series will go. If the Rays can tax the bullpens, they could be set up for success once the series heads to Tampa Bay. They'll need their own pitchers to play great, but if the Rays' offense can force the pitch counts of Henderson and Misiorowski to go high early in their respective starts, they could be set up for success in the World Series against the Brewers. item.title: African midfielder confirms he's ready to join Liverpool
item.description: African midfielder confirms he's ready to join Liverpool An exciting midfielder has confirmed he is ready to join Liverpool. The Reds are desperate to get back to the very top of domestic and European football. There was a time when the Reds were the team everyone feared under Jurgen Klopp, capable of going toe-to-toe with anyone and winning the biggest prizes in the game. But those days feel like a distant memory now. The foundations of that legendary side are slowly disappearing, and the next 12 months could mark the end of an era at Anfield. Virgil van Dijk, Joe Gomez and Alisson Becker are all approaching the final months of their current contracts. These are players who have been central to Liverpool's success over the years, but there are genuine questions about how much longer they will remain at the club. Liverpool's exciting plans for the future The Reds cannot afford to stand still. If they want to challenge for the Premier League and Champions League again, they need to build a squad capable of competing at the highest level for years to come. That's where Andoni Iraola and Julian Ward come in. The pair are tasked with shaping Liverpool's next great team, bringing together a new generation of talent with a clear tactical identity and a recruitment strategy that makes sense for the long term. Iraola will be expected to establish an intense, aggressive style of football that gets supporters excited again, while Ward must ensure the squad has the right balance of quality, experience and potential. It's an enormous challenge, particularly with so many key figures potentially heading towards the exit. But Liverpool have an opportunity to get this rebuild right. The Klopp era may be over, but that doesn't mean the Reds cannot reach those heights again. The real test is whether Iraola and Ward can turn that ambition into reality and make Liverpool a dominant force once more. Lamine Camara confirms he's ready to join Liverpool with stunning performance One of the biggest components of Liverpool's rebuild will be to bring in a midfielder. Liverpool simply need a dominant defensive-minded midfielder who can solidify the middle of the park and make Iraola's side less vulnerable to counterattacks. And the Reds should be looking no further than Lamine Camara. The Senegalese midfielder who was previously named African Young Player of the Year has been heavily linked with the Reds. Coming up against Freiburg on Thursday evening he confirmed just why the Reds want him and why he is absolutely ready to join Liverpool. Camara was voted as the Man of the Match in the game. He scored a wonderful goal arriving into the box and also won the most duels (9) and was the most fouled player (5) on the pitch while completing 55/65 passes and making nine passes into the final third. It was the perfect performance that showed he is ready for that move to Anfield. Julian Ward just needs to make it happen.

item.title: F1 United States GP: Charles Leclerc pips Max Verstappen to top FP1
item.description: Motorsport photo Ferrari driver Charles Leclerc pipped Red Bull's Max Verstappen to top first practice at Formula 1's United States Grand Prix in Austin. Leclerc was just under a tenth faster than Verstappen in an upgraded Ferrari as he aims to deny the Dutchman and his in-form Red Bull team a hat-track of grand prix wins. On a hot Circuit of the Americas, Ferrari hit the ground running as it trialled its latest, and understood to be the final, round of 2026 aero upgrades. The update package for Texas features revisions to the floor, bargeboard, sidepod and diffuser. While impressive sounding on paper, the team was keen to play down expectations, calling it a minor improvement. Whatever the case, Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton quickly managed to get up to speed in the early running on the undulating 5.5km circuit, with Leclerc's 1m36.61s on medium tyres 0.074s off Hamilton's first personal best. McLaren's Lando Norris was third ahead of Mercedes duo Kimi Antonelli and George Russell , who donned the slower hard compound for their opening runs and shipped four and five tenths respectively. Feedback on balance issues permeated the airwaves at COTA, which typically is a tough circuit to get right due to its varied track layout and bumpy surface. Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing Just after the halfway mark, Leclerc took seven tenths off his previous benchmark as he switched to the softest tyre compound. Mitigating early balance and steering rack woes, Verstappen shot up the timesheets to take second, 0.084s behind Leclerc's 1m36.052s lap. Verstappen's Red Bull, which featured an additional update to its new front wing, looked particularly impressive through COTA's first sector and its fast and flowing Esses. A lap that would see the four-time world champion usurp Leclerc was scratched for track limits at COTA's penultimate corner. After suffering a couple of snaps of oversteer, Norris took third 0.245s behind, ahead of Russell as the top four teams all appeared in the same ballpark based on FP1's limited sample size. World champion-elect Antonelli settled for fifth ahead of Hamilton and Piastri. Gabriel Bortoleto led the midfield in the Audi , taking eighth-place and just under a second off the pace of the frontrunners. That was slightly quicker than Arvid Lindblad in the Racing Bulls car, which has been comfortably leading the battle for fifth in the constructors' championship. Liam Lawson held off Haas driver Oliver Bearman to round out the top 10, while Aston Martin showed glimpses of improvement as Fernando Alonso and Lance Stroll took 12th and 13th. That put the pair ahead of Isack Hadjar in the second Red Bull, who lost his one-lap run due to exceeding track limits. FP1 featured one rookie runner in Cadillac's Colton Herta, who took the reins of Sergio Perez's car on home soil. item.description: Milwaukee Brewers third baseman David Hamilton The Milwaukee Brewers and Tampa Bay Rays will play Game 1 of the World Series on Friday. Both teams play a similar style of baseball, not relying on the long ball like most of the league. The Brewers were tied for 28th in the league in home runs and the Rays were ranked 22nd. However, both teams scored a ton of runs. The Brewers scored the second most runs in baseball, and the Rays scored the 12th most. They excel at what is seen as small ball, but it comes down to simply putting the ball in play. They were the top two teams in baseball in hits. According to MLB Network's Sarah Langs , it is the first time since 1964 that the teams that led their league in hits meet in the World Series. That season, the St. Louis Cardinals defeated the New York Yankees in the Fall Classic. Looking for the perfect gift for a baseball player in your life? On the other hand, the Rays strike out less than any team in baseball. While this series may not be full of superstars, there will still be plenty of action. item.description: At this point, calling Sunday a must-win game for the Rams feels almost redundant. Every week brings another chance to rescue their season. Every loss makes the next game more urgent. Every injury makes you wonder who will be available to do the rescuing. But there is another way to look at their visit to Allegiant Stadium, one that says as much about the team waiting for them as the battered group trying to hold itself together. This is a game the Raiders should win. They have earned the right for us to say that. Earned the expectations that come with it, too. Which makes whatever magic trick Sean McVay and Matthew Stafford are preparing all the more intriguing. And dangerous. In a city that has given us David Copperfield, Penn & Teller and countless other masters of deception, the Rams arrive needing a Houdini act to escape with a victory. The Raiders’ responsibility is to make sure nobody slips out of the handcuffs. Los Angeles Rams head coach Sean McVay, left, gestures during the first half of an NFL football game against the Arizona Cardinals in Inglewood, Calif., Sunday, Oct. 18, 2026. AP Photo/Gregory Bull That represents a meaningful change for a franchise that spent too many years serving as somebody else’s opportunity to get right. The Raiders were the soft landing. The manageable assignment. Now the Rams are 2-4 and wobbling , their depth chart resembling a MASH unit, and the Raiders should be expected to take advantage. Consider what McVay and Stafford are working around. Davante Adams is on injured reserve . So is nose tackle Poona Ford, sidelined by a triceps injury. Defensive lineman Kobie Turner is out for multiple weeks. Pass rusher Myles Garrett remains on injured reserve with a knee injury. Cornerback Trent McDuffie missed consecutive practices with a groin injury. Linebacker Nate Landman is in concussion protocol. Then Puka Nacua left Thursday’s practice with a calf injury. That does not automatically rule him out Sunday. But potentially losing him, or having him at less than full strength, further complicates life for an offense already missing Adams. Their red-zone execution has cost them touchdowns. Too often, their first-half momentum never makes it out of the halftime locker room. Their defense has surrendered too many explosive plays.. Yet they took the Chiefs and Bills into the 12th round at Allegiant Stadium, trading punches with two AFC heavyweights before losing the football equivalent of split decisions. Kansas City escaped 30-27. Buffalo survived 33-30. Six combined points separated the Raiders from two victories that would have dramatically changed the conversation. Give them an opening, and suddenly everyone is wondering how the guy escaped the locked box. The Raiders have earned the right to be expected to win this game. item.title: Julian Nagelsmann will accept Man United job on one condition, has already rejected two clubs for same reason
item.description: Julian Nagelsmann will accept Man United job on one condition, has already rejected two clubs for same reason Michael Carrick was visibly emotional during his pre-match press conference on Friday. Carrick will lead Manchester United against Bournemouth at Old Trafford on Sunday. However, given the way his side have been performing in recent weeks and the manner in which players such as Lisandro Martinez and Bruno Fernandes have publicly criticised the club’s hierarchy and the head coach’s tactics, a major change appears to be inevitable. Manchester United eyeing Julian Nagelsmann According to The Telegraph , pressure is mounting on Michael Carrick, with Manchester United already considering their options if they are forced to make a change. It is understood that former Germany and Bayern Munich boss Julian Nagelsmann will be a leading candidate to replace Carrick at United. Eddie Howe, who left Newcastle United in the summer, would also be high on the club’s shortlist due to his Premier League experience. Aston Villa’s Unai Emery, Brighton manager Fabian Hurzeler, and Antonio Conte also have admirers either at United or among figures connected to the club. Man United manager contenders wary of dressing room unrest It is claimed that “more than one of the candidates to potentially replace Carrick at United believe one of the biggest priorities would be to bring the dressing room into line.” A source close to one of United’s managerial candidates said: “It’s clear they need order and discipline. The dressing room is out of control and that is the first thing to fix.” Nagelsmann, who is out of work and immediately available, would listen to an approach if a change is made at Old Trafford. However, the 39-year-old German tactician would want “assurances over the structure above him, having pulled out of the running for the Tottenham Hotspur and Chelsea jobs in the past over that issue.” A separate report has suggested the club’s director of recruitment, Christopher Vivell, favours Nagelsmann, while Wilcox prefers Howe.

item.title: Nick Woltemade explains why he took penalty instead of Kolo Muani
item.description: Nick Woltemade explains why he took penalty instead of Kolo Muani Randal Kolo Muani is Juventus’ designated penalty taker, but when the Bianconeri were awarded a spot kick against Rennes last night , Nick Woltemade stepped forward to take responsibility and successfully converted the opportunity. His goal provided a positive moment for the German forward, who continues to build his record in European competition. Woltemade has now scored in every Europa League game he has played for Juventus since the start of the season, with two of those goals coming from penalties. Maintaining that scoring record will be encouraging for the striker, particularly as he looks to develop greater confidence and establish himself as an important member of the team. Confidence can make a significant difference to a forward’s performances, and finding the net against Rennes should help Woltemade. However, Kolo Muani also needs goals to strengthen his belief and make the most of his opportunities. Both players will want to contribute regularly as Juventus look to improve their attacking performances. Kolo Muani allows Woltemade to take the penalty Kolo Muani would also have welcomed the chance to score against Rennes after experiencing frustration in Juventus’ previous match against Lazio. The Frenchman had an early goal ruled out and failed to score again as the Bianconeri suffered a 3-0 defeat . After that disappointment, finding the net against Rennes could have helped him regain some momentum. Nevertheless, when Juventus were awarded a penalty, he allowed Woltemade to take the kick instead, giving his teammate an opportunity to add another goal to his European record. The decision proved successful, with Woltemade converting the spot kick. It also demonstrated that the forwards could work together and support each other, even when both have reasons to want a goal for themselves. (Photo by Valerio Pennicino/Getty Images) Woltemade explains his conversation with Kolo Muani The German striker has now revealed that he personally asked Kolo Muani for permission to take the penalty. He explained how the Frenchman responded and expressed satisfaction with his performance, as quoted by Football Italia : “I politely asked Kolo Muani if I could take the penalty, and he told me to go ahead. It went well and I scored. “At the end I would have liked to get a third. The most important thing is to play a good game. Tonight I played with the right spirit, and we’ll carry on like that.” Woltemade’s comments show that he was eager to contribute even more, despite being pleased with his display. The goal should provide a confidence boost, while Juventus will hope both forwards continue to find opportunities to score in their upcoming matches.

item.description: The Colorado Avalanche (5-3-1) return home for one game to host the Tampa Bay Lightning (7-2-0). Puck drop is scheduled for 7:08 p.m. MT. When he was finally ready to return, his father, Myles, passed away and O’Connor took a personal leave to be with his family. He has been skating with the team for several days and will slot in on the fourth line with Parker Kelly and recent call-up Taylor Makar . Mackenzie Blackwood makes his eighth start in 11 games to open the season. The Avs’ starting netminder is 4-3-0 with an .889 save percentage. In his last three games, Blackwood is 2-0-1 with a .915 save percentage. This will be his first time facing the Lightning since his days with the San Jose Sharks. The Lightning are off to a hot start, going 7-2-0 through nine games. They are 5-0 at home and 2-2 on the road, but are riding a three-game winning streak heading into this matchup. Nikita Kucherov leads the team with 13 points in nine games, while Brandon Hagel has seven goals and 12 points. Andrei Vasilevskiy gets the nod in goal. He has won six of eight games against Colorado since the 2022 Stanley Cup Final. item.title: Ben Johnson shares heartbreaking news on Cole Kmet injury
item.description: Ben Johnson shares heartbreaking news on Cole Kmet injury originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . It didn't take long for Chicago Bears head coach Ben Johnson to confirm the worst possible scenario for Cole Kmet. The tight end is out for the season. On Friday, Johnson spoke to the press about Kmet's situation and confirmed what many feared would be the case. Kmet is being placed on injured reserve and won't be able to take the field again this season. Ian Rapoport, an NFL insider for ESPN and the NFL Network, shared the news on X . "Coach Ben Johnson just said that Cole Kmet is headed to IR today due to his serious knee injury," Rapoport stated. "It is season-ending, with Johnson saying, 'He's a big part of our heartbeat. It stinks. I hate it.'" Cole Kmet's injury leaves the Chicago Bears with a big hole to fill The Bears beat the New England Patriots on Thursday Night Football, 30-24, and Kmet was on the field for most of the matchup. However, he left the game late due to a knee injury that looked nasty. Kmet's night took a bad turn midway through the fourth quarter when he injured his knee after making an eight-yard reception. The tight end was eventually taken off the field on a cart and transported to the locker room, but not before giving the Soldier Field crowd a thumbs-up. While that gesture was sweet, losing Kmet was still a significant concern for Chicago, and it will be for the rest of the season. After the game, Johnson said that the team would conduct a detailed evaluation of Kmet's injury on Monday. He also said, "I don't think it looked very good." With Kmet out, Colston Loveland will take on more responsibility, as will third-round rookie Sam Roush. item.title: Bayern Munich coach Kompany hospitalized after collapsing
item.description: Bayern Munich coach Vincent Kompany gestures on the touchline during the UEFA Champions League soccer match between Bayern Munich and Arsenal at Allianz Arena. (is associated with: «Bayern Munich coach Kompany hospitalized after collapsing») Peter Kneffel/dpa Bayern Munich coach Vincent Kompany is in hospital in Munich after collapsing at their training centre, the club has confirmed. "Vincent Kompany required medical attention after collapsing during an FC Bayern reserve team training session on Friday. The first-team head coach was watching the second string's session," a Bayern statement said. "Kompany is undergoing thorough examinations in hospital and will remain under medical care. His coaching staff will oversee training and match activities until further notice." The confirmation came after the Bild paper and Sky TV said that the 40-year-old was taken to hospital in an ambulance. "Vincent Kompany's health is our top priority. We at FC Bayern will do everything we can to ensure he makes a speedy recovery. Vinnie is receiving all the necessary medical care and support, and all the time he needs," board member for sport Max Eberl said in the statement. "His coaching team, whom we trust completely, will take over his duties. All of us at FC Bayern wish Vinnie a speedy recovery," Eberl added. Assistant Aaron Danks is expected to oversee their Bundesliga match on Sunday at Freiburg. Viral infection and hip problems Kompany had recently been suffering from a viral infection and had hip problems. On Tuesday, he sat out the final training session ahead of the Champions League match against Arsenal to rest, and was also absent from the mandatory press conference, with Danks standing in. However, Kompany was at the stadium to coach Wednesday night's match. After the draw against the English champions, Kompany said: "As a manager, you always want to do everything and give it your all. I caught quite a nasty virus last week; naturally, I didn't listen to my body, and at some point my body just said: 'Right, that's enough now!'" Watching Bundesliga match from a seat Kompany was already feeling unwell during the 6-1 Bundesliga win against RB Leipzig last Saturday and could only watch the match while seated on the Bayern bench. According to Bild, Kompany had to lie down briefly on a sofa at the Allianz Arena at half-time and after the match. "He's been battling a virus all week, which has been taking its toll on him," said Eberl, who stood in for Kompany at the press conference and in post-match interviews. "He really isn't feeling well." Kompany had therefore already missed training last Monday. item.title: Cristiano Ronaldo scores for Al Nassr after Portugal punishment
item.description: FILE PHOTO - Portugal's Cristiano Ronaldo reacts after the 2026 FIFA World Cup group K soccer match between Portugal and DR Congo at Houston Stadium. (is associated with: «Cristiano Ronaldo scores for Al Nassr after Portugal punishment») Tom Weller/dpa Cristiano Ronaldo scored for the first time since he was suspended by the Portuguese Football Federation when he helped Al Nassr to a 3-1 victory over Al Faisaly in the Saudi Pro League. The 41-year-old jumped highest from a free-kick and headed home from Joao Felix's delivery to put his side 2-0 up four minutes after the break. Ronaldo was handed a 30-day suspension and fined €255 ($286) this week after he walked out on his national team earlier this month following a row with head coach Jorge Jesus but put it behind him by getting on the scoresheet. Ronaldo is now 18 goals away from reaching the landmark milestone of 1,000 in his career after notching his sixth of the season. Al Nassr's 3-1 victory helped them keep up with Al Qadsiah and Al Hilal in the race for the title and handed them an eighth league win this term.

item.title: Legendary LSU basketball Coach Dale Brown dies
item.description: Legendary former LSU basketball Coach Dale Brown died Friday, Oct. 23. He was 90. Brown remains LSU's winning all-time coach with 448 wins and two NCAA Final Four appearances, though he was known as much for his motivational abilities as much as for his coaching acumen. He said players need to know you care before they care what you know. He was called "Daddy Dale" by opponents as an insult, but his players and fans embraced the nickname as a celebration of Brown's compassion and term of endearment. Brown came to LSU in 1972 and coached the team for 25 seasons. His death comes just two days after LSU announced he had been selected to receive the 2027 John R. Wooden Legends of Coaching Award recognizing his accomplishments and impact on college basketball. Brown led LSU to four Southeastern Conference regular-season championships and 13 NCAA Tournament appearances as well as the Final Four in 1981 and 1986. Among his most famous players is NBA Hall of Famer Shaquille O'Neal. Adoption angels: Speaker Mike Johnson honors Shreveport couple as 'Angels in Adoption' Brown was the Associated Press National Coach of the Year in 1981 and SEC Coach of the Year four times. He is a member of the National Collegiate Basketball Hall of Fame, Louisiana Sports Hall of Fame and LSU Athletic Hall of Fame. The court inside the Pete Maravich Assembly Center is named after Brown and former LSU women's coach Sue Gunter. item.title: Donald Trump: NFL ‘could have probably postponed’ Paris game
item.description: Credit: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images Despite pushback from President Donald Trump, the NFL is moving forward with its game in Paris as France experiences civil unrest. The NFL’s International Series continues Sunday, with the Saints and Steelers playing at Stade de France . The game is slated to take place despite civil unrest in France stemming from student-led protests over poor school conditions. The protests have escalated into widespread anti-government demonstrations, and in some cases, led to dangerous riots. Trump was asked about the game while addressing reporters outside the White House Friday morning, and the president suggested he would have advised the league to move the “match.” Trump: “I would’ve said the NFL could’ve probably postponed that match” (It’s called a game, not a match) https://t.co/k31201IoVK — Aaron Rupar (@atrupar) October 23, 2026 “It’s looking like tomorrow’s going to be a bad day in France, so you worry about it,” Trump said. “I would have said the NFL could have probably postponed that match, if you want to know the truth, because France is really in trouble.” Earlier this week, Boomer Esiason noted that the NFL claims there is no concern about the area hosting Sunday’s game. But Esiason wondered whether the game might attract social unrest . “They claim where they are going that there is no unrest,” Esiason said. “But if you want to amplify your unrest, the best way to do it would be around an NFL football game in France. It is ugly over there right now, and it’s basically uncontrolled… I don’t necessarily know that the French government has the stones to put it to rest. But right now, it’s about as bad as it’s ever been.” According to The New York Times, last weekend saw nearly 1,500 shops and retailers damaged by riots, with more than 2,400 arrests being made. Paris police instituted a curfew Monday night from 11 p.m. to 6 a.m. Tuesday morning and have since extended it through the week and into the weekend. With France anticipating more demonstrations this Saturday, several major tourist attractions and Paris museums, including the Louvre, announced closures for this weekend. Paris Saint-Germain’s Ligue 1 match against Lyon has also been postponed until Monday after police prohibited it from taking place on its originally scheduled date and time of Sunday at 8:45 p.m. The Saints have been in France since Monday for the game, with the Steelers arriving Thursday. The Steelers have already canceled their fan event in Bastille “as a precautionary measure.” But the NFL has maintained that the game will go on. item.title: Germie Bernard’s production is here to stay for the Steelers
item.description: (Photo by Parker S. Freedman/Getty Images) | Getty Images When the Pittsburgh Steelers traded up to select Alabama wide receiver Germie Bernard 47th overall in the second round of the 2026 NFL Draft, the image of the Steelers on the phone with USC wide receiver Makai Lemon before the Philadelphia Eagles jumped the Steelers to select the receiver just the night before was still fresh on everyone’s minds. Fast forward to Week 7, and Bernard has captured the attention of the NFL world. Pittsburgh made it a point to add to their receiver room this past offseason, as they traded for Michael Pittman Jr. from the Indianapolis Colts back in March. Despite the high draft capital investment the team made in him, Bernard found himself buried as the WR4 on the Steelers depth chart to start the season. After injuries to both Pittman and Roman Wilson, though, Bernard has had to step up in their absence and has exceeded all expectations. Bernard is second among all rookies in catches through six weeks with 24. He is just five receptions behind number four overall pick Carnell Tate for the most among all rookies. What sticks out the most is the fact that Bernard has 17 of his 24 catches over the last two weeks. With Pittman and Wilson both on injured reserve for an undetermined amount of time, Bernard is already making the most of his role. Quarterback Aaron Rodgers praised the rookie for his confidence that has clearly grown over the past several weeks after his breakout 11 reception 87 yard performance against Tampa Bay in which the rookie receiver scored the game-winning touchdown in overtime. “There comes a time when the confidence starts to match the potential, and I think we’re reaching that time with Germie,” Rodgers said. “Very proud of him.” Aaron Rodgers on Germie Bernard: "There comes a time when the confidence starts to match the potential, and I think we're reaching that time with Germie. Very proud of him." — Mike DeFabo (@MikeDeFabo) October 18, 2026 For someone who has the reputation of not trusting his rookie receivers enough, Rodgers has certainly shown a good bit of confidence in Bernard over the last few weeks as he continues to pepper him with targets. Not only does Rodgers seem to be trusting Bernard more and more, but the passing volume of the Steelers offense also bodes well for Bernard’s role the rest of the season. Rodgers’ 233 passing attempts through six weeks is the fifth most by any quarterback in the league. The veteran quarterback’s ADOT currently ranks 22nd in the league with a 7.3 mark . Bernard excelled in those short and intermediate areas of the field and after the catch in college. His play style translated seamlessly int the Steelers offense, coupled with the sheer amount of opportunities he could see, should have all Steelers fans excited. So much to get excited about with Germie Bernard's game. Dude is already a smooth and savvy football player who knows how to set up his defenders at the top of his routes. #Steelers pic.

item.title: Football Daily | Mourinho is ready for his clásico return – stock up on popcorn, folks!
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! Football Daily has never had much time for conspiracy theories. Lee Harvey Oswald dunnit, Stanley Kubrick didn’t fake the moon landing, Vinícius Jr doesn’t have a body double and Miranda isn’t a secret traitor. But our Spidey senses picked up when the UK government announced their Be Ready campaign on Thursday night. In case you missed it, or live outside the UK and couldn’t care less about this weird little island, we’ve lifted this from our news story : “Every Briton is being urged to stock up to nine litres of bottled water and three days’ worth of food in new government guidance designed to ensure that households can survive a weather, cyber or other serious emergency. The Be Ready campaign is aimed at persuading people to stock up with supplies to last 72 hours, amid growing official concern about the impact of the climate crisis, technological dependency and hostile state threats.” Would it not be much easier all round if the two big clubs in Manchester simply swapped all playing and coaching staff before the next round of fixtures? United would finally get the squad that Bruno Fernandes and Lisandro Martínez clearly feel they deserve, one of serial winners who are worthy of the club’s fine history (and free of the whiners). Meanwhile, City would might get a team that would make them (somewhat) competitive in the lower tiers where they’re surely headed. And a manager who has coached there quite recently. Sure there’d be a few grumbles from the fans, but more importantly in the current football climate, think of all the potential new shirt sales, and the Us-Against-the-World mentality that Enzo Maresca would be able to instil in his team whose own supporters would even hate them. And no-one would even have to move house. It’s a win-win solution. Although, no, it’s United; so probably a win-high-scoring-draw-against-Wycombe solution” – Justin Kavanagh. Like all right-minded people, I only read Big Website to get my fill of news and information (ahem …). However, I did come across a recent piece in The New Yorker on James Daunt, the chief suit of the US book chain Barnes & Noble (no relation). The billionaire Russian oligarch, Alexander Mamut, asked him 20 years ago how much it would cost to buy Waterstones, and when he was told it would be £40m, he looked pleased and just said, ‘That’s less than Fernando Torres’, before adding, ‘It’s not even half a boat’. Odd reference points these billionaires” – Noble Francis. May I be the first of 1,057 Daniels to say thank you for the good luck message at the end of Thursday’s Football Daily. It has put a little extra pep in my step today” – Daniel Mee. This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. item.title: Is el clásico still the world’s biggest match? Three questions before Barcelona v Real Madrid
item.description: The fixture’s relevance waned as the Messi-Ronaldo rivalry faded. Can Lamine Yamal and Mbappé lift it into a new era? For the best part of a decade, el clásico was more than just soccer’s biggest fixture. It was the defining narrative. At the peak of the Lionel Messi v Cristiano Ronaldo era, there were clásicos everywhere. Yes, when the two historic rivals clashed on the pitch, but also in the voting for the Ballon d’Or every year and in so much of the discourse around the sport. As the Messi-Ronaldo rivalry faded, though, so too did the clásico ’s relevance. This isn’t to say matches between Barcelona and Real Madrid no longer matter. They always have and always will. In 2026, however, it’s difficult to measure a clásico ’s standing. Is it still the sport’s biggest fixture? Continue reading...

item.title: Chaotic state of football in Brazil epitomises a nation where greed has conquered glory | Jonathan Liew
item.description: The national game merely reflects the mood in a divided nation which is going to the polls with very little faith in the power of democracy Look, cards on the table: I don’t know for certain, and nor do you, whether Flávio Bolsonaro – the man widely tipped to become the next president of Brazil after Sunday night’s election – really did steal an island from Richarlison. There are lawyers involved, claims and counter-claims, and in any case, adjudicating land ownership disputes between right-wing strongmen and Tottenham reserve-team strikers lies very much beyond this column’s spectrum of expertise. It’s why, for example, this newspaper took no official position on the well-publicised battle between Rodrigo Duterte and Vincent Janssen over that Polynesian isthmus. According to Richarlison, a few years ago he purchased an island off the southern coast of Rio de Janeiro, and has the documentation to prove it. Richarlison says Bolsonaro tried to buy it from him, and when he refused a lawyer named Willer Tomaz simply turned up and annexed it. “These guys took the island without spending a penny, as far as I know,” Richarlison claimed in an Instagram video that has been viewed more than 31 million times. Tomaz has accused Richarlison of lying, arguing that he has a public deed registered at the notary’s office. Bolsonaro, for his part, has denied any connection with the island in question and described Richarlison’s intervention as “politically motivated”. Continue reading...

item.title: Premier League: 10 things to look out for this weekend
item.description: Max Dowman may get a chance, Spurs need to find balance at Stamford Bridge and Axel Disasi must make amends Premier League top scorers After seven games, Nottingham Forest’s record is eerily similar to last season: five points, five goals scored. A year ago Forest’s eighth game was a 3-0 home loss to Chelsea that marked the end for Ange Postecoglou , the second of four managers to occupy the dugout last term. There is no suggestion that Oliver Glasner is under similar scrutiny yet, but the Austrian needs to find solutions for the league’s lowest scorers. Morgan Gibbs-White is available after missing the narrow defeat by Arsenal , while Liam Delap may benefit from a return to familiar surroundings – 12 of his 14 career Premier League goals were scored for Ipswich, six of them at Portman Road. “What we need to improve is getting [Delap] into more positions where he can score,” Glasner said before Friday evening’s game. “He’s one of our best finishers.” Gary O’Neil also lacks a standout scorer, but he is squeezing goals out of his side. Eight different Ipswich players have scored in seven games; only Brighton and Brentford can better that total this season. item.title: Bournemouth enjoy night to remember as 10-man Milan fail to weather storm
item.description: This was a momentous night in Bournemouth’s history, although the truth is they would have been given a far sterner examination by Coventry or Hull. Whatever this rotten impersonation of a Milan side was, it bore no relation to those that forged such a celebrated history. The visitors resembled holograms even before their goalkeeper Mike Maignan, with an extraordinary rush of blood resulting in a penalty and red card, rendered their task impossible. They never showed the slightest hint of putting up a fight. Bournemouth simply swamped the seven-time European champions and, amid a swirling south coast storm that rarely let up, could depart singing in the rain. Amine Adli’s sumptuous late free-kick, curled left-footed from 22 yards, meant they could finish the evening with the flourish they deserved. Their joy was clear at full time and met disapproval from some of Milan’s staff, who appeared to take umbrage in a short-lived fracas near the tunnel afterwards. Continue reading...

item.title: Manchester City have been a joy to watch but they became detached from their roots | Philipp Lahm
item.description: City behaved much like other top clubs but their rule-breaking deserves to be punished. The Bundesliga, where members have a controlling stake, can show the way forward Do we have to reassess Manchester City now? In my columns, I have repeatedly engaged with this club and its key figures. Looking back at what I have written over the years, I believe it remains beyond question that the team have achieved greatness. I always loved watching them: they were a true unit on the pitch, a finely tuned orchestra. I would also write all over again that the conductor, Pep Guardiola, masters his craft like few others. I could recognise his teams even if they were wearing the wrong shirts and the game was broadcast in black and white – by the passes, the distances between the players and the intelligence of their interplay. It is no wonder Guardiola inspires others to become managers; look at Vincent Kompany, Mikel Arteta, Enzo Maresca, and perhaps some time Ilkay Gündogan and Rodri. Continue reading...

item.title: Too much Overlap? Gary Neville’s podcast empire knows no bounds
item.description: The Overlap has gone daily, with Steven Gerrard and Joe Hart among the latest additions to an ever-growing family Viewed in 2026, Nathan Barley, Chris Morris’s 2005 sitcom, shows remarkable prescience about the last two decades of metropolitan life, from smartphone addiction and digital derangement to sheer existential vapidity. When Barley’s character referred to his occupation as “self-facilitating media node”, Morris and co-writer Charlie Brooker were way ahead on the creator economy. What the pair failed to predict was ex-footballers joining the sector in droves. These days, if you are a former footballer without a podcast or YouTube channel, then did you ever really play the game? Setting aside the Gary Lineker Goalhanger empire, manspreading its centrist-dad agenda into issues way beyond guffaws with Micah Richards and Alan Shearer, there is Gary Neville to rule them all. Manchesterism’s second-most influential practitioner has been on heavy manoeuvres. Unlike Lineker’s productions, the Overlap’s output continues to stick largely to football; a rugby podcast was mothballed in February, though its cricket equivalent continues. Continue reading...

item.description: The four Premier League clubs playing in the lesser continental competitions face each other on Sunday – but three are struggling domestically The sun shone. Not only that, but you could sit anywhere you wanted in a stadium too big for the game and, if you happened to have gravitated to the comfortable hospitality seating at the back of the lower tier, the beer was inexplicably free. Locals in Leiria seemed bewildered but could hardly have been more accommodating. A beer pump had been installed outside a patisserie on the Praça Francisco Rodrigues Lobo, whose owner soon found fans happy to help stack empty barrels if that facilitated the free flow of Sagres. “There was a meeting at the town hall to explain these are not hooligans,” said the owner of a radical leftist flammkuchen restaurant between the square and the cathedral. “They told us the club comes from the labour movement and I found that very interesting.” And how had she found the fans? “Noisy, but with a quirky sense of humour.” Continue reading...

item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

item.title: Martínez has drawn back the curtain on Manchester United’s ruinous ownership | Jonathan Liew
item.description: Defender may not be blameless in team’s struggles but his criticism goes to the heart of what has gone wrong at the club Heartbreaking: the worst defender you know just made a great point. And no, nobody would describe Lisandro Martínez as the ideal person to scrutinise Manchester United’s indifferent start to the season , given that his high-profile defensive errors against Fulham and Tottenham are partly responsible for it. “We’re all trying to find the guy who did this,” Martínez burbles on Amazon Prime after United’s 2-0 defeat by Atlético Madrid on Tuesday night, dressed in a hot dog costume and throwing his arms out in mock innocence. For those with no interest in engaging with what Martínez actually had to say, this alone will be sufficient grounds to ignore him. Already you can sense the squeamishness of former players for whom the violation of an omertà is the real cardinal sin here, a phantom limb that still tingles years after they last stepped into a dressing room. “Disrespectful,” reckoned Wayne Rooney. “I don’t feel like he’s got the right,” agreed Ashley Young. “These things don’t end well, man,” Rio Ferdinand observed on his podcast. item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...
